implementation_notes: CPython's type system has no sum type, so the pattern collapses into ordinary values: two frozen dataclasses (or NamedTuples), a Union for the checker, and an isinstance chain or - from 3.10 - a match statement with class patterns, which narrows the Union inside each branch. The language's own answer to the same situation remains try/except, and the returns library supplies a full Result with bind/map and a @safe decorator when the composition machinery is wanted. The hand-rolled version earns its place when the failure is a value that has to travel through several layers rather than an event that stops the current call.
pitfalls: match is not exhaustiveness-checked and simply does nothing when no case matches: keep the Union closed for the checker and end the match with a case that raises AssertionError for the impossible branch.
Frozen dataclasses are only shallowly immutable - a mutable payload (list/dict) still leaks mutation through Ok, and an unhashable payload silently breaks using the value as a dict key.

Conversion helpers that swallow the exception (try: int(text) except ValueError: return None) throw away the reason the pattern exists to carry; convert once, at the boundary, and keep the exception as the reason.
Exceptions still arrive from the stdlib and third-party code inside the same function, so a function that returns Ok/Err and also raises gives callers two channels to handle.

variants.name: returns Result with bind and @safe
variants.implementation_notes: The returns library documents Result as Success(value) or Failure(error) with map/bind/alt composition, a @safe decorator that turns a throwing function into one returning Result, and pattern matching through PEP 634 class patterns. Choose it when a pipeline of fallible steps is the shape of the code, since bind enforces that every step returns a Result and keeps the error type stable; the library's mypy plugin is required for full type inference, which is a real adoption cost.
pitfalls: @safe catches Exception (not BaseException) and stores it unchanged, so the reason type is whatever was raised - a domain reason has to be raised and caught, not returned.
Typing only works fully with the library's mypy plugin (a documented limitation): without it the checker infers Result[float, Any] in places and the contract weakens silently.
bind enforces a single error type across the chain; steps that fail with different exceptions need unify() or an explicit Union, otherwise the composition does not type-check.
